result.summary: This PR replaces the Logger class's three separate fields (a category bitmask, a global log level, and a hash map of per-category level overrides) with a single small array of atomic per-level category bitmasks, dropping seven now-redundant methods (EnableCategory, DisableCategory, WillLogCategory, LogLevel, SetLogLevel, GetCategoryMask, AddCategoryLogLevel). It touches call sites in RPC, kernel, GUI, and interfaces::Node that used the old API, and adds tests documenting the change. One intentional, documented behavior change remains: categories enabled at runtime via the logging RPC or the kernel API are now always enabled at Debug level rather than preserving a previously-set Trace level from -loglevel.
result.problem: The Logger class's redundant, multi-field representation (bitmask + global level + mutex-protected hash map) makes the logging code harder to follow and makes simple operations like changing a category's level require coordinating several fields and methods, a burden felt by anyone maintaining or extending logging.

open_concerns: l0rinc questioned whether Trace/Debug-only conditional levels mixed with unconditional Info+ levels is the right long-term model; author responded but left the design question open as a matter of preference, not blocking.

result.card: This PR replaces Bitcoin Core's Logger internal state (a category bitmask, a global log level, and a mutex-guarded per-category level map) with a single small array of atomic bitmasks, dropping seven redundant methods, and is described by the author as behavior-preserving except that runtime category enabling via the logging RPC or kernel API now always uses Debug level instead of a previously-set Trace level. It is a maintainability improvement to shared logging infrastructure used by every area, plus small follow-on changes to the RPC, kernel API semantics, and kernel build (CMake export fixes for CI link failures on Windows/shared builds). The sole reviewer (l0rinc) raised substantial concerns across two CHANGES_REQUESTED rounds about commit granularity and two unintended behavior regressions, all of which the author addressed with commit splitting, fixes, and new tests, though no re-review has occurred since May 2026 despite continued rebases through August. No stated hard dependency exists, but the author's own conflict list and commentary suggest this is groundwork for the related #35387 trace-logging PR.
